partners.diseaseBName: combined immunodeficiency due to ORAI1 deficiency
partners.mechanism_chain: ITPR2 (HGNC:28606) —DISRUPTS→ calcium signaling (GO:0005886); calcium signaling (GO:0005886) —LEADS_TO→ anhidrosis (HP:0009085); ORAI1 (HGNC:29807) —DISRUPTS→ calcium signaling (GO:0005886); calcium signaling (GO:0005886) —LEADS_TO→ combined immunodeficiency (HP:0002695). Loss-of-function mutations in ITPR2 impair calcium release, contributing to anhidrosis. Concurrently, loss-of-function mutations in ORAI1 impair store-operated calcium entry. Both pathways converge on dysregulation of intracellular calcium signaling, ultimately leading to the distinct phenotypes of anhidrosis and combined immunodeficiency, respectively.

partners.mechanism_chain: ORAI1 (HGNC:17857) —DISRUPTS→ Store-operated calcium entry (SOCE) (GO:0034398); Store-operated calcium entry (SOCE) (GO:0034398) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal sweat gland function (HP:0003410); Store-operated calcium entry (SOCE) (GO:0034398) —LEADS_TO→ Myopathy, tubular aggregate (MONDO:0014383); ITPR2 (HGNC:6152) —DISRUPTS→ IP3-mediated calcium release (GO:0006143); IP3-mediated calcium release (GO:0006143) —DECREASES→ Store-operated calcium entry (SOCE) (GO:0034398). Loss-of-function mutations in ORAI1 directly impair store-operated calcium entry (SOCE). Reduced SOCE affects calcium homeostasis in various cell types. In eccrine glands, this leads to impaired sweat secretion (anhidrosis). In skeletal muscle, dysregulated calcium handling, potentially secondary to impaired SOCE and/or altered IP3-mediated calcium release due to ITPR2 dysfunction, contributes to the formation of tubular aggregates and myopathy.
